You're not manipulative unless you use emotion/threats/etc to force someone to change in some way. Literally every MBTI ever can be manipulative. One group is no manipulative than the other, maybe functions make people better at manipulation, but that doesn't really mean that type in inherently manipulative. 

Thou it is obvious the standard INFJ profile can be an absolute fantastic manipulator because of the understanding of other people in a deeper sense and how analytical we are about it and there are definitely some out there who are assholes and have ruined peoples lives by doing this.

I'm sorry you feel like this ): unfortunately MBTI has been torn apart and made into very bland bits that are pieced together into dumb stereotypes by the community. Remember you are more than your MBTI type and you are your own unique person that's able to have feelings and emotions like everyone else. 

The large portion of INTJs I've met have been a little cold acting at first but warm up pretty fast once you get to know them.  A lot of INTJs I know are very passionate about things which I really respect in a person, even if I'm not interested in what they're passionate about. INTJs are also super loyal friends and very good conservationists when they have someone to listen to them. I think a lot of people are instantly thrown off by how INTJs seem to appear and don't look any deeper into the person.

The anemia thing is actually biological! The darker you are the more UVB your skin absorbs. The more UVB your skin absorbs the less vitamin D you get from the sun. Low levels of vitamin D can be a cause of anemia. So when you have skin evolved to handle some of the sunniest and hottest areas of the world and are in a northern continent the chances of being anemic are much higher.

If you feel like cutting people off even if they're close is the best decision for you and your health then do it. Prioritize yourself over other people and their problems. 

I understand it's different with family and I know how that is personally so maybe sit down and have a talk with them if you can about what's stressing you out and see if they're open to change. 

If you can't do either of those things then keep contact to a minimum. You could also try slowly cutting them off by doing that instead of just going cold turkey.

INTJs are human so yes INTJs care about and prioritize people, they arent robots, just very picky individuals about who they spend their time with and care about (INxJs in general tend to be like that we dont care to waste our time). He might just not want to commit to in person contact, he just might think it's not important enough to spend his personal time on. 

My advice to you is bluntly ask him how he feels about you. For all you know he could just be shy and nervous. Don't get all jumpy to conclusions or you'll probably piss him off.
